# How to Prepare for Your Next Job Interview Using Free AI Tools

**Hook:** Preparing for a job interview can feel overwhelming, but you do not have to do it alone. This guide will show you how to use free AI tools as a personal, non-judgemental mock interviewer to help you practice your answers and calm your nerves.

## Before you start
- **Choose an AI tool:** Open any free AI chatbot, such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini. Think of an AI chatbot as a highly responsive digital conversationalist powered by an LLM (large language model—the smart software engine that processes and generates text).
- **Have your materials ready:** Copy the text of the job description you are applying for, along with a draft of your current resume.

## Step 1 — Extract the key interview questions
Instead of guessing what an employer might ask, you can ask the AI to analyse the job description to find the most likely questions. To do this, you will write a prompt (the written instructions or questions you type into an AI tool).

💬 **Example prompt to copy and paste:**
> "I am interviewing for a job. Here is the job description: [Paste Job Description]. Based on this, what are the top 5 questions the interviewer is most likely to ask me? Please explain why each question is important."

## Step 2 — Research the company's culture
To stand out, you need to show that you understand the employer's values and mission. You can use the AI to identify core themes, which will help you tailor your language to match their workplace culture.

💬 **Example prompt to copy and paste:**
> "I want to make sure my answers align with this company's values. Here is some text from their 'About Us' page: [Paste About Us Text]. Can you identify the top 3 cultural values they care about, and suggest how I can show I have these traits?"

## Step 3 — Set up a mock interview roleplay
This is where the magic happens. You can ask the AI to act exactly like a friendly, professional hiring manager. It will ask you one question at a time, wait for your response, and then give you constructive feedback.

💬 **Example prompt to copy and paste:**
> "I want you to act as an interviewer for the role described earlier. Ask me one practice question at a time. After I reply, give me friendly feedback on how to make my answer stronger, then ask the next question. Let's start with the first question."

## Step 4 — Polish your stories using the STAR method
Employers love structured answers. The AI can help you organise your past experiences using the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result—a classic, easy-to-follow formula for telling clear stories about your work history).

💬 **Example prompt to copy and paste:**
> "Here is an experience I want to share in my interview: [Type a rough, messy summary of a past work achievement]. Can you help me rewrite this using the STAR method so it sounds professional and clear?"

## Step 5 — Calm your pre-interview nerves
Anxiety often comes from a fear of the unknown. You can ask the AI for advice on handling difficult, unexpected questions, or even ask it to share a quick, calming breathing exercise to help you focus.

💬 **Example prompt to copy and paste:**
> "I am feeling quite nervous about my interview tomorrow. Can you give me three simple strategies to stay calm if I get asked a question I do not know the answer to?"

## Common mistakes
- **Trusting made-up facts:** Sometimes AI can hallucinate (a term used when an AI confidently presents incorrect details as truth). Always double-check facts about the company on their official website.
- **Sounding like a robot:** Use the AI's suggestions as a guide, but do not memorise its responses word-for-word. Employers want to hire *you*, complete with your unique personality and natural speaking style.
- **Sharing private information:** Never paste highly sensitive details into public AI tools, such as tax file numbers or private client details from your previous workplace.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You will build stronger communication skills, helping you feel more confident when speaking to new people or presenting ideas.
- **For your business or work:** You can easily prepare for internal promotions, salary reviews, or client pitches in a fraction of the usual time.
- **If you're just getting started:** Treat the AI like a patient, encouraging mentor. You can make mistakes in a completely private, safe space before speaking to a real person.

## Try it now
Open your chosen AI tool, copy the text below, and press send:

> "I have an upcoming interview for a customer service role. Can you give me one common interview question for this type of job, and a simple tip on how to answer it well?"
